deck.title: DAMA-DMBOK Chapter 1 — Data Management Study Summary

slides.title: Data Management Goals
summary: Understanding and supporting the information needs of the enterprise and its stakeholders, including customers, employees, and business partners
Capturing, storing, protecting, and ensuring the integrity of data assets
Ensuring the quality of data and information
Ensuring the privacy and confidentiality of stakeholder data
Preventing unauthorized or inappropriate access, manipulation, or use of data and information
Ensuring data can be used effectively to add value to the enterprise

slides.title: Section 2 — Essential Concepts: Overview
summary: 2.1 Data — what data is, representation, context, and the disciplines required to manage it
2.2 Data and Information — the DIKW pyramid, its limitations, and why both data and information must be managed
2.3 Data as an Organizational Asset — data as economic resource; value, monetization, and the data-driven organisation
2.4 Data Management Principles — 12 foundational principles grouped in four themes
2.5 Data Management Challenges — 13 challenges that arise from the properties and principles of data
2.6 Data Management Strategy — strategy components, deliverables, and the CDO's role

columns.heading: Nature of Data
bullets: Represents facts about the world; in IT, also understood as information stored in digital form — though data is not limited to digitised information
A means of representation: 'stands for things other than itself' (Chisholm, 2010)
Both an interpretation of objects it represents and an object that must itself be interpreted (Sebastian-Coleman, 2013)
Context = data's representational system; the conventions of that system are documented as Metadata

columns.heading: Why Management is Needed
bullets: People make different choices about how to represent concepts, creating multiple shapes for the same idea
Even within one organisation, different departments represent the same concept differently
Across organisations, the problem of multiplicity multiplies, requiring industry-level data standards
Multiplicity drives the need for Data Architecture, modeling, governance, stewardship, and Metadata and Data Quality management

slides.title: Why Data Representation is Complex
slides.intro: Different choices about how to represent concepts create compounding challenges that require dedicated management disciplines.

steps.label: Representation choices
steps.detail: People choose how to represent concepts; no single agreed method exists for complex entities such as 'customer' or 'product'

steps.label: Multiple shapes
steps.detail: From different choices, data takes on different shapes and forms — even within the same organisation

steps.label: Multiplicity grows
steps.detail: Across departments and organisations, multiple representations of the same concept multiply

steps.label: Disciplines required
steps.detail: Drives the need for Data Architecture, modeling, governance, stewardship, Metadata and Data Quality management

columns.heading: The DIKW Pyramid
bullets: Data is called the 'raw material of information'; information is called 'data in context'
A layered pyramid is often used: Data → Information → Knowledge → Wisdom
Useful for explaining why data needs to be well managed
Throughout the DMBOK, 'data' and 'information' are used interchangeably

columns.heading: Three Challenges with the Pyramid
bullets: It assumes data simply exists — but data has to be created
Its linear sequence fails to recognise that it takes knowledge to create data in the first place
It implies data and information are separate — in reality they are intertwined and dependent on each other
Central tenet: BOTH data and information need to be managed together with uses and customer requirements in mind
